name: Cyrus
bio:
Cyrus, king of Persia, conquered Babylon and its empire. In his first year, to fulfill the LORD's word spoken through Jeremiah, the LORD stirred his spirit to issue a proclamation throughout his kingdom: the LORD God of heaven, who had given him all the kingdoms of the earth, had charged him to build a house for him in Jerusalem, and any of God's people were free to go up and do so, with the LORD their God with them (2 Chronicles 36:22-23). This decree, which opens the return from exile, is told in fuller detail in the book of Ezra.

Ezra tells what followed: the heads of the families of Judah and Benjamin, the priests, and the Levites — everyone whose spirit God had stirred — rose up to go rebuild the LORD's house in Jerusalem, while their neighbors helped them with silver, gold, goods, livestock, and freewill offerings. Cyrus also had the temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar had carried off from Jerusalem brought out of the Babylonian temple where they had been kept; his treasurer Mithredath counted them out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah — 5,400 gold and silver articles in all, which Sheshbazzar brought up with the returning exiles (Ezra 1:5-11).

 Over a century before his birth, Isaiah named Cyrus by name in prophecy, calling him the LORD's shepherd and anointed one who would order Jerusalem rebuilt and the temple's foundation laid, and whom the LORD would strengthen to subdue nations and break down gates of bronze and bars of iron, calling him by name though Cyrus did not yet know him (Isaiah 44:28-45:4).
